Fix what the output names. Move the tasks it touches to in_progress with UpdateTask while you work and to tested once their tests pass; leave the rest of the board as it is.

Reproduce the failure with a run narrowed to the test the output names, fix it, then run that test again and build its project. The whole sweep runs again as soon as you stop with every task tested, so stopping on a fix you have not run costs another one.

CodeOutline on the failing test's file gives the line each test starts on: Read that test's range rather than the whole file.

What earlier tasks left:
- Rules that became optional [tested]: `withInstructionFiles(mode, systemPrompt, cwd, home)`, `instructionsText(files)`, `CLASH_WITH_CORE` and `wantsInstructions(mode)` in src/agent/instructions/instruction-files.ts: the one join point where the workspace's and the person's instruction files (and, once later tasks write them, applied bundles) reach a session's prompt, for every mode but the blind planner, with a note telling the model a rule already given always wins and to say which instruction-file rule it set aside. `ModeContext.withInstructions` (src/agent/session/mode-setup.ts) wires it into every non-chat, non-plan mode, wrapped outermost in session-engines.ts's `modeContext()`. The chat prompt on both engines (buildSystemPrompt and session-engines.ts's startClaude) now also joins instruction files through the same `instructionsText`/`CLASH_WITH_CORE`. To avoid a duplicate copy of the person's own memory notes (which live inside their instruction file), `MemorySources`/`memorySection`/`withMemories`/`chatMemorySection` in src/agent/memory/session-context.ts now carry the project's index only; the person's own notes ride the instruction files wherever those join, on both engines. (files: src/agent/instructions/instruction-files.ts, src/agent/openai-session/system-prompt.ts, src/agent/memory/session-context.ts, src/agent/session/mode-setup.ts, src/session-engines.ts, plan/agents-md-rule-bundles.spec.md, test/mode-setup.test.ts, test/system-prompt.test.ts, test/memory-session-context.test.ts, test/instruction-files-session.test.ts)
- Picking up bundles for a workspace [tested]: src/agent/instructions/bundles.ts: `Bundle`, `BundleScope`, `BundleTarget`, `AppliedBundle`, `BundleCatalogPort`, `WorkspaceSignals`; `bundleFilePath(scope, cwd, home)` (project → `<cwd>/AGENTS.md`, user → `<home>/AGENTS.md`, never CLAUDE.md); the marked-block mechanics `applyBundleText`, `removeBundleText`, `parseAppliedBundles`; the file-backed `appliedBundles`, `applyBundle`, `removeBundle`; the workspace probe `workspaceSignals` (languages from source/project file extensions the repo map already walks, frameworks from package.json dependencies and .csproj PackageReferences) and `bundleMatches`/`matchingBundles`. src/settings/settings-store.ts: `BundlePort` (available/matching/applied/apply/remove, closed over a workspace the same way `MemoryPort` is), `SettingsStore.applyBundle/removeBundle/dismissBundleOffer`, `SettingsSnapshot.bundles` (available, applied, suggested, offerPending) computed from `bundleOfferDismissed` plus the port. src/settings/webview/bundles-tab.ts: `BundlesTab` custom element, the 'bundles' SettingsTab, and events `BundleAppliedEvent`/`BundleRemovedEvent`/`BundleOfferDismissedEvent` in events.ts, wired in settings-app.ts and settings-panel.ts. The `BundlePort` wired in extension.ts has `available()` stubbed to an empty catalog; `matching()`, `applied()`, `apply()`, `remove()` are already real, so the next feature only has to replace `available()` with real git sources. (files: src/agent/instructions/bundles.ts, src/settings/protocol.ts, src/settings/settings-store.ts, src/settings/settings-panel.ts, src/settings/webview/bundles-tab.ts, src/settings/webview/events.ts, src/settings/webview/settings-app.ts, src/extension.ts, test/bundles.test.ts, test/settings-store.test.ts, test/settings-app.test.ts, test/models-section.test.ts, test/profiles-tab.test.ts, test/providers-tab.test.ts)
- Where bundles come from [tested]: src/agent/instructions/bundle-sources.ts: PRODUCT_CATALOG_SOURCE, bundleSources/pendingSources/fetchableSources (person+workspace source lists, acceptance gate), parseCatalogSource + CATALOG_FILE ('bundles.json', rule text only — any command/tool/permissions/settings field is read off an entry but never kept), GitPort + the real gitPort (plain `git clone --depth 1`, no credentials of its own) and SourceCachePort + fileSourceCache (last-fetch fallback under `<home>/.kiwi/bundle-sources/`), FetchedSource/fetchSource (fetch-or-fall-back-to-cache), RequiredBundle/requiredBundles/missingRequiredBundles/requiredBundleText/applyRequiredBundles (auto-applies a source's required bundles for the project, first time and again if removed), isNewerVersion, HandEditCheck/BundleUpdate/bundleUpdates/hashBundleText (update detection remembering a declined version per bundle, and hand-edit detection by comparing a block's current text to the hash of what was last written). src/agent/instructions/bundles.ts: new `appliedBundleText` reads one applied block's current body, and `Bundle` gained an optional `asOf`. src/extension.ts wires `BundlePort.available()` to real fetched sources (`kiwiAgent.bundleSources` for the person, `kiwiAgent.projectBundleSources` for the workspace, `kiwiAgent.bundleSources.accepted` for acceptance) and runs a once-per-activation check — with a real project open only — that offers each pending source, applies missing required bundles, and offers each available update (remembering hand-edit hashes in `kiwiAgent.bundleHashes` and declined versions in `kiwiAgent.bundleUpdatesDismissed`, both workspace-scoped) through native VS Code notifications, since this scenario carries no dedicated settings-page surface of its own. (files: src/agent/instructions/bundle-sources.ts, src/agent/instructions/bundles.ts, src/extension.ts, test/bundle-sources.test.ts, test/bundles.test.ts)
- Moving from CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md [tested]: src/agent/instructions/claude-md-move.ts: claudeMdPath(scope, cwd, home) (BundleScope reused: 'project' → <cwd>/CLAUDE.md, 'user' → <home>/.claude/CLAUDE.md), mergedAgentsText(claudeText, existingAgentsText) (whole text when AGENTS.md was empty, appended under a "## Moved from CLAUDE.md" heading otherwise), PendingMove and pendingMove(scope, cwd, home) (what a move would write, using bundles.ts's bundleFilePath as the AGENTS.md destination so it is the same file a bundle writes into), moveOfferDue(move, alreadyDeclined), applyMove(move) (writes AGENTS.md, removes CLAUDE.md). src/agent/memory/memories.ts: userMemoryFile(home) now resolves to <home>/.claude/CLAUDE.md while it still exists, falling back to <home>/AGENTS.md once it is gone (by the move or because the person never had one), so a person-scope memory follows the same file the move carries their instructions into. src/extension.ts wires a once-per-activation offer (native VS Code modal, 'claudeMdMoveDismissed' workspace-scoped for the project, 'claudeMdMoveDismissedUser' global for the person) that shows the merged text and, on confirmation, calls applyMove; not narrowly testable (no vitest harness for extension.ts in this repo, matching the earlier bundle-sources offer wiring). (files: src/agent/instructions/claude-md-move.ts, src/agent/memory/memories.ts, src/extension.ts, test/claude-md-move.test.ts, test/memories.test.ts)

event.text:
The sweep failure was not in any task's code: `vitest.config.mts` carried `isolate: false` (an old workaround for a worker spawn-storm flake), and on vitest 5.0.3 that makes every test file fail before its first test — the exact `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')` / `Vitest failed to find the runner` pair in the output, reproducible on a single file and gone with `--isolate`.

I dropped `isolate: false` back to per-file isolation (replacing the stale comment with why sharing a worker is not an option), re-ran the feature's own test files (13 files, 251 tests, green), typechecked the project clean, and ran the whole suite: 120 passed, 3 skipped, 1597 tests, 8.9s. "Rules that became optional" is back to tested with `vitest.config.mts` added to its files and the reason in its note; the other three tasks were untouched and their tests pass as they stand.
